subject: game_design

resources.title: Game Design
resources.notes: Practical design and analysis of games through team projects, rules design, iteration and extensive playtesting.

resources.title: Game Design
resources.notes: Historical and analytical game-design course with original game projects, documented testing, mechanics analysis and iteration.

resources.title: Learn to Build Your Own Videogame with the Unity Game Engine and Microsoft Kinect
resources.notes: No prior programming or game-design experience required; guided and team projects cover videogame creation, Unity, GitHub collaboration, 3D objects, gesture input and team management.

resources.title: Creating Video Games
resources.notes: Multidisciplinary teams design, develop, test and focus-test original digital games; emphasizes iteration across design, audio, aesthetics, fiction, programming and production.

resources.title: Introduction to Videogame Studies
resources.notes: Interdisciplinary study and analysis of videogames; no programming prerequisite, with additional work for graduate students.

resources.title: Computer Games and Simulations for Education and Exploration
resources.notes: Students design games and examine learning outcomes, research/development issues and field testing.

resources.title: Game Design and Game Technology Research Discovery
resources.notes: Research discovery only; individual papers require provenance, evidence-quality, version and license verification before use.

known_gaps: Dedicated beginner curricula for game AI and advanced game programming remain thinner than core design and production coverage.
Graduate and research-level game-design expertise requires item-level research evidence, current production practice and assessment rather than repository discovery alone.
Accessibility coverage should be strengthened with dedicated authoritative game-accessibility standards and practical testing resources.
